_readme: OWNER APPROVAL LIST FOR PHOTO-DERIVED LOCATIONS.
Every pin on the public footprint map, and every 'documented project' cited
on a regional domain, is derived from GPS coordinates inside photographs.
Nothing distinguishes a photograph of a driveway you paved from a photograph
of a house you stayed in. Four times now, personal locations have reached the
public site because the pipeline assumed a cluster of photographs meant work:
three of the owner's own homes, and a family visit to the Outer Banks that was
published as ten job sites with coordinates on a public map.
This file is the owner's say-so, in writing. scripts/verify-photo-approvals.mjs
enforces it during the build.
HOW TO USE IT
denied    Never publishable. If one of these turns up in jobSites.json the
BUILD FAILS. This is what stops a removed location coming back
through a re-import.
approved  Confirmed by the owner as real work, safe to publish.
mode      'warn'   - unreviewed locations still publish, and the build
prints how many are awaiting review.
'strict' - ONLY approved locations publish. Anything unreviewed
fails the build. Switch to this once the review queue
is worked through.
Identity is the rounded coordinate pair, not the city name, because a city
label can be re-geocoded but the coordinates in the photograph cannot.
SCOPE LIMIT, stated honestly: this guards build-time data (jobSites.json).
Gallery photographs served from the backend API at runtime are NOT covered
here and need the same treatment on the backend before they can be trusted.
